notes: Synthetic. Truth is what each line does at run time, except where a policy turns it into a gap. boto3 is followed only to clients built for the service "bedrock-runtime" (here as a literal, also through boto3.Session(...).client), and a Bedrock request's model is its modelId, for any model Bedrock serves, so every such call routes bedrock. gateway is given an endpoint_url outside AWS, so it and its converse_stream are custom_base_url (the URL itself is never output). The s3 client storage and its put_object are not tracked. bedrock_runtime.py:31 reads modelId from the environment: no value, an env_var gap. session_client.py passes its client and model to a public function, so the route keeps an in_file_callers gap and the model is a parameter gap listing what the one in-file caller passes. ChatBedrock and ChatBedrockConverse are LangChain chat models on Bedrock: each constructor is a client and a call record with its model (model_id= or model=), and invoke on the built model keeps its routing. BedrockEmbeddings and its embed_documents are not tracked. LiteLLM is followed only through completion and acompletion: litellm_calls.py:15 passes the model by position, through a module constant; litellm.drop_params is a setting, not a patch, and litellm.token_counter is not a request.
